standard_prerequisites: Context span 792-805 (section-non-abelian): for R a ring and I finitely generated, the category A of I-adically complete R-modules has cokernel of phi: M -> N given by the I-adic completion of the usual cokernel (Algebra, hathat-finitely-generated) and kernel the usual kernel, which is closed and I-adically complete by Lemma closed-is-complete (delivered card L48284)

Context span 1161-1201 (section-nonabelian-QCoh): X = Spf(Z_p) with the p-adic topology is a sheaf in sets on (Sch/Z)_fppf and gives a stack in setoids (Stacks, when-stack-in-sets); quasi-coherent modules on it correspond to systems (M_n) of abelian groups annihilated by p^n with M_n = M_{n+1}/p^n M_{n+1}, equivalently to the p-adically complete abelian group M = lim M_n with M_n = M/p^n M (Algebra, limit-complete); the category of quasi-coherent modules on X is thus equivalent to the category of p-adically complete abelian groups, which the context states is not abelian, see Section non-abelian
core_obligations: Quasi-coherent modules on X = Spf(Z_p) are equivalent to p-adically complete abelian groups (context)

In the complete category the cokernel is the completion of the usual cokernel while the kernel is the usual kernel (context span 792-805); completion of cokernels is not exact in general (the completion-failure examples of the same chapter, delivered as L48306), so image and coimage need not agree and the category is not abelian
X is a Noetherian affine formal algebraic space, proving the lemma
proof_roadmap: Identify QCoh(X) with the complete category via the context equivalence
Read the kernel and cokernel formulas from the section-non-abelian span
Conclude non-abelian-ness from the completion failures already in the unit pool
